steps.q: Does it make a great product or service?
Will it keep earning above market profits?

views.text: In March 2021, Equity Mates explained that Sydney Airport held a local monopoly with high capital costs, creating high barriers to entry and defensible, long‑lived assets that supported predictable cash flow.

episode.title: EM Chat: Industry Deep Dive - Infrastructure

views.text: In February 2018, Equity Mates described Sydney Airport as a bond proxy with consistent air traffic and the ability to set prices as the only airport in Sydney, highlighting durable demand and pricing power.

steps.q: Can it reinvest its profits productively?

views.text: In February 2023, Equity Mates noted companies like Sydney Airport rewarded shareholders with dividends, contrasting them with growth companies that reinvested profits.
In February 2018, Equity Mates characterised Sydney Airport as paying a consistent amount every half year, like a bond proxy, signalling a focus on regular dividends to shareholders.

steps.q: Can it be bought at a reasonable price?

views.text: In July 2021, Equity Mates covered a takeover offer at $8.25 a share for Sydney Airport, compared to $5.81 before the news, and said the price jump reflected the market repricing on the bid.

episode.title: Why did Sydney Airport take off? ... and much more...
